items.title: Doctors in Ukraine Try Treating Infections Like Biological Warfare Attacks
items.author: Gina Kolata and Marc Santora
items.content: <article>As many as 40 percent of injured soldiers face severe infections that can lead to amputations and death. One initiative is trying to fix that.</article>

items.title: Iran Braces for More War, No Matter the Outcome of the U.S. and Israeli Elections
items.author: Yeganeh Torbati
items.content: <article>With Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu fighting to stay in power and President Trump facing a tough midterm, Iran’s leaders expect no major shift in policy.</article>

items.title: Syria Weighs Joining Saudi Mutual Defense Pact as Yemen War Rages
items.author: Euan Ward and Vivian Nereim
items.content: <article>A move to join Saudi Arabia’s agreement with Turkey and Pakistan could entangle more countries in the kingdom’s escalating conflict between the Iran-backed Houthis.</article>

items.title: Evacuees Arrive to Safety From Besieged Ukrainian City of Oleshky
items.author: Carlotta Gall and Oleksandr Chubko
items.content: <article>A few days of truce allowed the removal of remaining civilians from Oleshky, which continual Russian attacks have made all but uninhabitable.</article>

items.title: The NYC Marathon Is as Popular as Ever. It Remains Inaccessible to Many.
items.author: Santul Nerkar
items.content: <article>Running has long been celebrated as a cheap and accessible sport. But the culture of racing, especially in New York, is often anything but.</article>

items.title: Brace Yourself for an ‘Unusual Election’
items.author: Robert Siegel, Jamelle Bouie, E.J. Dionne Jr. and Vishakha Darbha
items.content: <article>Democratic sweep or not, politics are about to change.</article>

items.title: Republicans Tried to Turn the Cheesecake Factory Against Democrats. It Flopped.
items.author: Michelle Goldberg
items.content: <article>It’s become screamingly obvious who represents billionaires and unchecked plutocratic power.</article>

items.title: Martin McDonagh Says Art Can Change the World. Just Not as Much as Murder.
items.author: David Marchese
items.content: <article>The writer-director, known for his dark and bleak work, believes in film’s power to change our lives.</article>

items.title: Why Haley Stevens Can’t Stop Talking About Abdul El-Sayed
items.author: Reid J. Epstein
items.content: <article>In a frank interview, she described her disappointment and also said she was considering converting to Judaism. Her fiancé had thoughts, too.</article>

items.title: Beware of Election Night Mirages
items.author: Christine Zhang, Laura Bult, Brian Oh and Stephanie Swart
items.content: <article>Early race counts on election night can sometimes differ sharply from the final outcome. Christine Zhang, our election data reporter, explains the reasons behind red and blue “mirages.”</article>
